title: lebre: online forecasting with statistically tested structural changes
description:
Installable Python library implementing LEBRE v0.53, an online one-step-ahead forecaster for a target driven by exogenous inputs, at a fixed per-step cost (median 919 floating-point operations per step in the final evaluation). It has three layers: a structural core (LEBRE v0.52-r1, unchanged) whose structural changes are accepted only when an anytime-valid e-process of predictive improvement crosses a level set by an online multiple-testing rule; M1, a precision expert combined with the core by AdaHedge; and M2, which starts the output from a declared trivial reference and combines two paths by an (A,B)-Prod. The core alone (identical to lebre 0.1.0) remains available.

LEBRE v0.53 was promoted by a pre-registered rule in the research record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23282527; https://github.com/Iquitim/lebre-research): on 104 reserved series its mean squared error was 0.955 of the core's (95% CI 0.951-0.960), with no harm in any family. In the reference environment (Windows, CPython 3.11, NumPy 2.2.5) its forecasts are bit-for-bit identical to the promoted research code.

Scope and limits. One-step forecasting; the gain came from basins and FX, with no gain in solar, wind and load; about twice the cost of the core; no formal guarantee in the original scale for M1 and M2; no component is original. See the research record for the full evidence and its limits.
